cohort: The study participants were child mothers aged 10-14 and teen mothers aged 15-19 in the United States, identified through national birth and fetal death datasets between 1982 and 2017.
finding: Childhood pregnancy (mothers aged 10-14) was modestly associated with an elevated risk for stillbirth compared to teen mothers (aged 15-19), despite overall declines in stillbirth rates for both groups.
